questions.problem:
Let $T:{R}^{3}\to {R}^{3}$ be a linear transformation whose standard matrix is $T.$ Which of the following statements are true?

I. If $\text{Im}(T)=\{[x,y,z]^{T}\,:\,y=z\}$ then $\text{nullity}(T)=1$

II. If $Tx=[1,-2,3]^{T}$ has no solution, then $\text{nullity}(T)=0$

III. If $\text{Im}(T)=\text{Span}\{[\begin{aligned}1 \\ -2 \\ 3\end{aligned}],[\begin{aligned}-3 \\ 6 \\ -9\end{aligned}]\}$, then $T$ is invertible
questions.worked_solution:
Since $T$ is a linear transformation from ${R}^{3}$ into ${R}^{3},$ the invertible matrix theorem states the following:

 $T$ is a bijection (an invertible transformation) $\,⟺\,\{\,\begin{aligned} & \text{Im}(T)={R}^{3} \\  & \text{rank}(T)=3 \\  & \text{Ker}(T)=\{0\} \\  & \text{nullity}(T)=0\end{aligned}$ 

Also, according to the rank-nullity theorem, 

$$
\text{rank}(T)+\text{nullity}(T)=3.
$$

With that in mind, let's examine each statement in turn.

- Statement I is true. Since $y=z,$ any vector from $\text{Im}(T)$ can be written as

$$
\begin{aligned}[\begin{aligned}x \\ y \\ z\end{aligned}]=[\begin{aligned}x \\ z \\ z\end{aligned}]=x{{[\begin{aligned}1 \\ 0 \\ 0\end{aligned}]}_{⏟}}_{{v}_{1}}+z{{[\begin{aligned}0 \\ 1 \\ 1\end{aligned}]}_{⏟}}_{{v}_{2}}.\end{aligned}
$$

This means that $\text{Im}(T)=\text{Span}\{{v}_{1},{v}_{2}\}.$ Therefore, $\text{rank}(T)=2.$ Finally, according to the rank-nullity theorem, we obtain

$$
\begin{aligned}\text{nullity}(T) & =3-\text{rank}(T) \\  & =3-2 \\  & =1.\end{aligned}
$$

- Statement II is false. Since $Tx=[\begin{aligned}1 \\ -2 \\ 3\end{aligned}]$ has no solution, this means that $[\begin{aligned}1 \\ -2 \\ 3\end{aligned}]\notin \text{Im}(T).$ Therefore, $\text{Im}(T)\ne {R}^{3}$ and, according to the invertible matrix theorem, $\text{nullity}(T)\ne 0.$

- Statement III is false. Notice that $\text{Im}(T)=\text{Span}\{[\begin{aligned}1 \\ -2 \\ 3\end{aligned}],[\begin{aligned}-3 \\ 6 \\ -9\end{aligned}]\}=\text{Span}\{[\begin{aligned}1 \\ -2 \\ 3\end{aligned}]\}.$ Therefore, $\text{rank}(T)=1.$ So, $T$ is not a bijection or, which is the same, $T$ is not invertible.

Therefore, the correct answer is "I only."

questions.problem:
Let $T:{R}^{3}\to {R}^{3}$ be a linear transformation whose standard matrix is $T,$ and let $\{{v}_{1},{v}_{2}\}$ be a set of linearly independent vectors in ${R}^{3}.$ Consider the following statement:

*If  $\text{Ker}(T)=\text{Span}\{{v}_{1},{v}_{2}\}$, then $\text{__________}.$ *

Which of the following can be placed into the blank space to make a true statement?

I. $\text{nullity}(T)=2$

II. $\text{rank}(T)=1$

III. $T$ is a bijection
questions.worked_solution:
Since $T$ is a linear transformation from ${R}^{3}$ into ${R}^{3},$ the invertible matrix theorem states the following:

 $T$ is a bijection (an invertible transformation) $\,⟺\,\{\,\begin{aligned} & \text{Im}(T)={R}^{3} \\  & \text{rank}(T)=3 \\  & \text{Ker}(T)=\{0\} \\  & \text{nullity}(T)=0\end{aligned}$ 

Also, according to the rank-nullity theorem, 

$$
\text{rank}(T)+\text{nullity}(T)=3.
$$

With that in mind, let's examine each statement in turn.

- Statement I is true. Since $\text{Ker}(T)=\text{Span}\{{v}_{1},{v}_{2}\}$ and the set $\{{v}_{1},{v}_{2}\}$ is linearly independent, we get that $\text{nullity}(T)=2.$

- Statement II is true. According to the rank-nullity theorem, we obtain 

$$
\begin{aligned}\text{rank}(T) & =3-\text{nullity}(T) \\  & =3-2 \\  & =1.\end{aligned}
$$

- Statement III is false. Since $\text{rank}(T)\ne 3$ (or since $\text{nullity}(T)\ne 0$), the linear transformation $T$ cannot be a bijection according to the invertible matrix theorem.

Therefore, the correct option is "I and II only."

questions.worked_solution:
Any vector from $\text{Im}(T)$ can be written as

$$
\begin{aligned}[\begin{aligned}2z \\ w \\ z \\ w\end{aligned}]=z{{[\begin{aligned}2 \\ 0 \\ 1 \\ 0\end{aligned}]}_{⏟}}_{{v}_{1}}+w{{[\begin{aligned}0 \\ 1 \\ 0 \\ 1\end{aligned}]}_{⏟}}_{{v}_{2}}.\end{aligned}
$$

This means that $\text{Im}(T)=\text{Span}\{{v}_{1},{v}_{2}\}.$ Therefore, $\text{rank}(T)=2.$ 

Finally, according the rank-nullity theorem, we obtain

$$
\begin{aligned}\text{nullity}(T) & =4-\text{rank}(T) \\  & =4-2 \\  & =2.\end{aligned}
$$

$$

This means that $\text{Im}(T)=\text{Span}\{{v}_{1},{v}_{2}\}.$ Therefore, $\text{rank}(T)=2.$ 

Finally, according to the rank-nullity theorem, we obtain

This means that $\text{Im}(T)=\text{Span}\{{v}_{1},{v}_{2}\}.$ Therefore, $\text{rank}(T)=2.$ 

Finally, according the rank-nullity theorem, we obtain

$$
